personas.name: Denise Okonkwo-Hart
personas.who: 44, operations manager, the designated computer person for her family. Handling her mother's insurance claim after a fall. Competent with software, no access needs, deeply suspicious of free document sites since her employer circulated the FBI advisory about malicious free file tools — the exact distrust the research names in emotionalContext.
personas.context: Locked-down Windows work laptop, 1280px window, trackpad only, no stylus, eleven minutes of a lunch break. The claim PDF is already open in the next tab. Overhead office light, someone talking to her.
personas.task: Get one transparent signature PNG and drop it into the claim form before her 13:00 call.
personas.verdict: Got the file in about four minutes and the file itself is genuinely good. She also lost her best attempt twice — once to a mis-tap and once to a reflex reload — and both losses were completely silent.
delights: No email field, no modal, no counter, no wait timer, no tip prompt anywhere on the export path. Eight rapid clicks on Download produced eight clean files with no double-submit corruption and no leftover DOM (verified: 0 residual a[download] nodes). After Signaturely's 'Sign 1 documents for free' footer this read as a different category of thing.

The output is exactly what the hero promised. Decoded pixel by pixel: 93.9% fully transparent, corner alpha 0, exactly one opaque colour — rgb(17,19,24) — plus 1,902 antialiased edge pixels, auto-cropped from a 942x780 buffer down to 632x216. It dropped onto the claim PDF with no white box, which is complaint #3 in the research solved properly.

Palm and stray-pointer rejection works. A second pointer arriving mid-stroke left 0 ink in the palm zone (measured). Resizing the window mid-stroke kept the stroke and resynced the buffer with no error.

frictions.what: Her fourth attempt was the good one. Reaching for Download PNG she hit Clear — the two are identical 316x44 full-width .btn elements stacked 8px apart at phone and narrow-window widths (measured at 390px: Undo 605-649, Clear 657-701, Download 709-753). Clear runs `strokes = []; current = null; redraw()` with no confirm, no toast, no undo. Measured: 1,773 ink pixels to 0, toast text empty, toast not shown, no undo button, and pressing Undo afterwards restores nothing.
frictions.whyItMatters: This is the one artefact in the whole portfolio the user cannot reproduce — the research says outright to assume 'the user is slightly embarrassed by how their mouse signature looks, and will draw it four or five times: undo, clear and redraw must be immediate and unjudgemental.' Instead the destructive control is styled identically to the primary one, sits 8px from it in the thumb zone, and is the only irreversible action in the app. sws-ui.js is loaded and window.SWS.undo exists (verified true at runtime); app.js never calls it once. .btn.danger is defined at index.html:580 and never used.

frictions.what: She hit refresh out of habit when the page felt stuck. Everything went. Measured: 1,092 ink pixels before reload, 0 after; localStorage holds 0 bytes and no keys for this app at any point.
frictions.whyItMatters: There is no autosave, no draft, no 'you have unsaved work' guard on beforeunload, and — worse — no sentence anywhere saying nothing is kept. The research asks for exactly the opposite of silence: 'This app never keeps your signature. Close the tab and it is gone. That is on purpose.' Right now ephemerality is an absent feature rather than a stated choice, so it reads as the app losing her work rather than protecting her. The standard battery reports this app as 'persisted' because it counts text characters; the artefact is a canvas, so the battery cannot see the loss.

frictions.what: Nothing tells her what she is about to get. She had no idea whether 633x218 was big enough for a form that would be printed. There is no dimension readout, no KB figure, no dpi note, no filename preview — and the same gesture exports at 633x218 at 414px and 1529x248 at 1280px.
frictions.whyItMatters: Research complaint #4 is Adobe's own documented Fill & Sign blur bug; the only defence the app controls is giving people more pixels than they think they need and saying so. The output resolution is currently an accident of the browser window and she cannot even see the number.

frictions.what: Every export is called signature.png. Her eight rapid clicks produced signature.png, signature(1).png … signature(7).png in Downloads.
frictions.whyItMatters: She could not tell which of eight files was the attempt she liked, and the button gives no busy state or debounce while the 72ms export runs.

personas.name: Marguerite Lavallée
personas.who: 71, retired school secretary. Macular changes in her right eye plus essential tremor in her writing hand. Uses an iPad daily, distrusts anything that looks like software. This is the comfort-panel persona.
personas.context: Her kitchen, 09:40, iPad in portrait at 414 CSS px propped against the fruit bowl, bright window behind it, one hand steadying the tablet and one finger drawing. Her daughter emailed a care-home admission form and is waiting on it. No hard deadline, very little patience.
personas.task: Sign the admission form and send the picture back to her daughter.
personas.verdict: She found the comfort panel unprompted and set it up correctly. It then made the app actively worse: the signing pad refused to grow, the Download button dropped below the fold, and — the part that made her stop — the ink stopped landing where her finger was.
delights: She found the gear beside the app name straight away, and the panel is a genuine fieldset of real radios with a permanent tick slot. axe on the open panel: 0 violations. Largest took the root font from 16px to 24px and the hint paragraph from 15px to 22.5px; page overflow stayed at 0px at both 320px and 414px.

The pad is a true white rectangle in dark mode too (verified: rgb(255,255,255) with the OS in dark), so the black ink she picked really is the black ink she gets. That is the right call and the research names it as a hard constraint.

frictions.what: After she set Spacing to Roomy, the pen started drawing to the left of her finger. Measured and isolated: setting density=roomy alone takes the pad's CSS width from 338px to 320px while the canvas backing store stays at 338 — fitCanvas() only runs on window resize (app.js:117), and a comfort-panel attribute change fires no resize event. Pen down at 288px into the pad, ink landed at 274px: a 14px offset, 4.9%, growing linearly toward the right edge. The signature already on the pad squashed 14px to the left at the same moment. It only corrects itself if the window is resized. Setting text=xxl or reading=easy alone does NOT trigger it — only Spacing does.
frictions.whyItMatters: With a tremor she is already fighting her own hand; a pen that is systematically 14px off is unusable, and she blamed herself. The one comfort dial most likely to be reached for by someone with a dexterity need is the one dial that breaks the core interaction, and the app's own hint tells her to 'sign larger than feels natural' — which pushes her toward the right-hand side of the pad where the error is worst.

frictions.what: The signing pad is the only thing on the page that does not respond to Largest text. Measured at 320px: pad 244x260 at Default and 244x260 at Largest; at 414px + Roomy it is 320x260. #pad is hardcoded `height:260px` (index.html:1257) and fitCanvas hardcodes `cssH = 260` (app.js:27). The signable band above the ruled line is 198px.
frictions.whyItMatters: She turned the text up because she cannot see small things. The single element on the page that she has to see and aim inside stayed exactly the same size, so the comfort setting made the pad proportionally smaller relative to everything else. On a 390px phone that is a 316x198px window to write a name in.

frictions.what: At Largest the Download PNG button falls below the fold. Measured: dlVisibleWithoutScroll false at 320px/xxl and at 414px/xxl+roomy (pad bottom 785 and 736 respectively in a 900px viewport, with the three buttons below that).
frictions.whyItMatters: The comfort setting she needs pushes the app's only output off screen. There is no sticky action bar — .actionbar is defined at index.html:805 and unused — so the button that finishes the job is the one thing Largest text hides.

frictions.what: She could not see where to sign. The ruled line is a hardcoded #d7dde5 hairline — 1.37:1 against the white pad — and the ✕ mark is #b9c2cc at 1.80:1. Turning Contrast to High changes neither, because both are literal hex values in the app layer (index.html:1258-1259) rather than tokens.
frictions.whyItMatters: The ✕-and-rule is the entire wayfinding of the signing surface, and it is the lowest-contrast thing on the page. High contrast raised the hint paragraph from 5.95:1 to 16.05:1 and left the two marks she actually needed at 1.37 and 1.80.

frictions.what: The two ink swatches are 30x30px, hardcoded, and never scale with text size (measured 30x30 at Default, at Largest, and at Roomy, on every viewport). They carry no aria-pressed and no visible state other than a box-shadow ring.
frictions.whyItMatters: 30px is 14px under the system's own --tap: max(44px, ...) floor at index.html:265, on a target she is aiming at with a shaking finger, right next to the other one. The Fine/Medium/Bold buttons are 32-33px at Default and only reach 43px at Largest.

frictions.what: She turned Warm tint to High for the glare from the window, and the signing pad turned peach. Measured: the pad renders as rgb(255,214,177) because body::after paints rgba(255,166,86,0.46) at z-index 9999 over everything including the hardcoded-white .padwrap. The ruled line drops to 1.01:1 and the ✕ to 1.33:1, and the blue ink swatch reads as navy-black.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research states this as a hard constraint that overrides fashion: 'the signing pad must be a true white rectangle in every theme, because it is a WYSIWYG preview of ink on a document — a tinted pad turns the exported ink colour into a guess.' Dark mode is handled correctly and warm tint is not. She is choosing an ink colour against a background the exported file will never have.

frictions.what: Inside the comfort panel, the 'Roomy' option can end up underneath the panel's own sticky footer and stop responding to taps. Measured at 414x900: dialog 736px tall, body scroll height 1,132px against a 576px viewport, footer top at y=740; with the body scrolled to bring Roomy just into view, the .sws-foot element sits over it and swallows the click (the automated driver retried for 30 seconds and never landed it).
frictions.whyItMatters: It is recoverable by scrolling further, but the first tap does nothing and gives no feedback, which for this user reads as the app being broken. The scroll container needs scroll-padding-bottom for its own sticky footer. This is a shared-chrome issue, not an app-layer one.

personas.name: Ilya Brenner
personas.who: 34, backend developer with severe RSI. Drives everything from the keyboard; a trackball comes out for maybe ten minutes a day and drawing is not one of the things he spends it on. Would use a switch on a bad week.
personas.context: Standing desk, Chromebook at 1280px, keyboard only, mid-afternoon, no time pressure and no tolerance for being told to use a mouse.
personas.task: Sign a freelance contract addendum so he can email it back before the client's day ends.
personas.verdict: Could not produce a signature. Not slowly, not awkwardly — there is no keyboard path to the app's only output at all.
delights: The tab order is short and completely orderly: Display settings → Tip jar → Black ink → Blue ink → Fine → Medium → Bold → Undo stroke → Clear → Download PNG → Sky Wolf Studio → Feedback → body. 12 focusables, 0 unreachable, 0 unnamed. Nothing is trapped.
Focus rings are real and legible: 2px solid rgb(96,113,149) at 2px offset, 4.77:1 against the card. There is a <main id="main"> landmark.
axe returned zero violations in every configuration tested — light, dark, warm tint 3, high contrast, Largest + Roomy, and after drawing. Zero console errors across the entire run.

frictions.what: <canvas id="pad"> at index.html:1291 has tabindex null, role null, aria-label null and zero fallback content, and drawing on it is the only route to an output. Verified at runtime. There is no typed path, no photo import, no file input and no drop target anywhere in index.html or app.js.
frictions.whyItMatters: A flat WCAG 2.1.1 failure on the app's single verb, and the research quotes Section508.gov and ADA practice naming typing and image upload as the required alternatives: 'There is no way to make a signature without a working pointing device, which is an ADA and Section 508 problem, not a nice-to-have.' Everything else in the app is keyboard-perfect, which makes it worse — he can select black ink, choose Bold, tab to Download, press Enter, and get a toast telling him to 'Sign above first.' The app is fully operable except for the part that produces the product.

frictions.what: The ink and pen controls communicate their state only through a CSS class. Verified: both .dot buttons and all three .sizes buttons have aria-pressed null and role null; selection lives entirely in `classList.toggle('sel', ...)` at app.js:105 and app.js:111.
frictions.whyItMatters: With a screen reader on he hears five buttons — 'Black ink, Blue ink, Fine, Medium, Bold' — and is never told which ink or which weight is currently active. They should be aria-pressed toggle buttons.

frictions.what: 'Fine', 'Medium' and 'Bold' have no group name. The word 'Pen' that labels them is a plain <span class="label"> (index.html:1299), as is 'Ink' (index.html:1296) — neither is a legend, a fieldset, an aria-label or an aria-labelledby target.
frictions.whyItMatters: Out of context 'Fine / Medium / Bold' could be anything. The two groups are visually labelled and programmatically anonymous.

frictions.what:
The ✕ guide mark is a live text node —
✕
at index.html:1293 with no aria-hidden (verified null).
frictions.whyItMatters: A screen reader reads a bare 'multiplication X' in the middle of the app's main region, where it means nothing without the visual context.

frictions.what: Undo stroke with nothing drawn is a completely silent no-op — `strokes.pop()` on an empty array (app.js:114). Measured: toast text empty, nothing announced. No control is ever disabled (undoBtn, clearBtn and dlBtn all report disabled false at every state), even though .btn[disabled] styling exists at index.html:1261.
frictions.whyItMatters: Three buttons that always look and announce as available, one of which does nothing and one of which destroys everything.

frictions.what: No skip link and no <noscript>. Verified: document.querySelector('.skip') is null and there is no noscript element, while the .skip component sits fully styled and unused at index.html:840-849.
frictions.whyItMatters: Minor here because the page is short, but with JS off the page renders a hero, a blank white rectangle and three dead buttons — indistinguishable from a broken site, on an app whose whole pitch is trustworthiness.

personas.name: Priyanka Deshmukh
personas.who: 22, final-year student, applying for an IBPS clerk post. Third application this month; two friends have already had forms rejected over the signature image. Knows the spec by heart because the portal shouts it at her: 140 x 60 px, JPG, white background, under 30 KB.
personas.context: Android phone at 390px in a hostel room at 23:20, one thumb, the application window closes at 23:59. Patchy wifi. She found this app because it looked cleaner than the ad-covered resizer sites.
personas.task: Produce a signature file the IBPS portal will accept, tonight.
personas.verdict: Produced a beautiful file the portal will reject on three counts, and the app never mentioned any of them. She went back to a resizer site with four ad banners on it.
delights: It worked with the wifi dropping out. The service worker (sig-v14) had all 10 assets cached; a full reload with the network cut still rendered, still drew, and still exported. That is the research's 'turn your Wi-Fi off, it still works' claim actually being true.
Nothing covered the pad or the export button at any point. The toast sits at the bottom (measured top 782 in a 900px viewport) and never overlaps the signing surface.

frictions.what: PNG is the only output. app.js:165 ends at `out.toDataURL('image/png')` and there is no format control anywhere. Her file came out 632x216 transparent PNG at 16.9 KB.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research's second complaint quotes the portals' own ranked rejection list, top of which is 'Format not JPEG — PNG is commonly rejected,' followed by 'Coloured background instead of white.' A transparent PNG is precisely the two things that get rejected, and this app produces nothing else. This is the highest-volume signature-upload workflow in the world and the app is 100% incompatible with it.

frictions.what: No dimension or file-size control and no readout. SCALE is hardcoded to 3 at app.js:123 over `pad.clientWidth`, so the output size is whatever her phone's viewport happened to be. Measured across viewports with the same gesture: 632x216 / 16.9 KB at 390px, 633x218 / 14.2 KB at 414px, 1529x248 / 34.5 KB at 1280px.
frictions.whyItMatters: She needs exactly 140x60 at under 30 KB. She cannot see any of those three numbers before or after download, cannot set any of them, and the 1280px case would have blown the 30 KB ceiling on its own. The research's whole 'own the export nobody else designs for' differentiator is a live px/KB readout plus named presets, and there is currently not even a readout.

frictions.what: She tapped once on the pad to test it, then hit Download. She got a 38x38 PNG of a single dot, 411 bytes, with a cheerful 'Saved — transparent background, cropped to the ink' toast. The only guard is `strokes.length === 0` at app.js:121.
frictions.whyItMatters: At 23:20 with a deadline, an app that confidently exports a 38px dot as your signature is worse than one that refuses. A minimum-ink or minimum-extent check costs nothing — trimBounds already computes the bounding box.

frictions.what: The signable area on her phone is 316 x 198 CSS px (measured at 390px: pad 316x262, ruled line 198px down from the top). The app's own hint tells her to 'sign larger than feels natural'.
frictions.whyItMatters: The advice and the interface contradict each other. The research asks for a full-bleed 'Sign big' landscape sheet; instead she is writing her name in a letterbox about a finger and a half tall, which is exactly the szimek/signature_pad complaint the research cites.

personas.name: Hal Brennan
personas.who: 58, small-business owner in Ohio. This week he is doing two things with the same signature file: a mortgage refinance package his title company wants signed in blue, and an I-130 petition for his wife. Confident with a computer, entirely unaware that either of those has rules about signatures.
personas.context: Home office desktop, 1280px, mouse, Sunday evening, reading glasses, unhurried. He has both documents open and intends to reuse one PNG for everything.
personas.task: Make one signature image and paste it into everything he has to sign this month.
personas.verdict: Got a clean file in two minutes and used it on both. The app was flawless and told him nothing that would have stopped him forfeiting a USCIS filing fee.
delights: Both inks export exactly as shown — verified: black is a single opaque rgb(17,19,24) and blue is a single opaque rgb(29,63,143), no colour drift, no fringing beyond the antialias band.

'Drawn and saved on your device — your signature never touches a server' in the hero, plus 'Runs entirely in your browser. Nothing uploaded, ever.' in the footer, was enough for him to keep going where a site with an email box would not have been.

frictions.what: Nothing anywhere in index.html or app.js says where a drawn signature is not valid. There is no warning block, no caveat, no .warn instance (the component sits unused at index.html:670).
frictions.whyItMatters: This is the research's number-one complaint and its number-one differentiator, and it is now time-critical: the DHS interim final rule published 11 May 2026 and effective 10 July 2026 lets USCIS reject OR DENY a filing found to lack a valid signature after it has cleared the Lockbox — keeping the fee, with no post-filing correction — and USCIS explicitly rejects signatures 'generated by software.' Signature-related denials went from 300 in FY2021 to 2,953 in FY2025. Hal is about to lose a filing fee and months of waiting because a free tool was polite. Every competitor's incentive is to get him to sign; ours is not, and this is the single most valuable thing that asymmetry buys.

frictions.what: He picked black because it was already selected, for a mortgage package where the title company expects blue. The two swatches carry aria-label 'Black ink' and 'Blue ink' and nothing else — no title, no caption, no explanation (verified: title null on both).
frictions.whyItMatters: The research is specific: blue proves an original against a photocopy and is 'not just preferred but functionally required by most lenders and title companies,' while exam portals mandate black on white. One clause per swatch turns a two-button picker into visible expertise. It is free, it is true, and it is the difference between his closing going through and being sent back.

frictions.what: There is no way to get the image anywhere except the Downloads folder. app.js:164-169 builds an <a download> and clicks it; there is no clipboard path, no Web Share, no 'place it on a PDF' handoff, and no initials.
frictions.whyItMatters: His actual goal is a signed document, not a PNG. The research notes Online PNG Tools reserves copy-to-clipboard for paying customers — which is exactly why it should be a first-class button here, and it costs one ClipboardItem call. The mortgage package also asked him to initial nine pages and he had to come back and draw a second, smaller mark.

frictions.what: He signed once, disliked it, and pressed Clear. Then he wanted the first one back. There is no redo, no history, no last-three-attempts strip.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research's own emotional read is that people draw this four or five times; keeping the previous attempts visible costs a few hundred bytes of geometry that is already in memory.

personas.name: Yusuf Adeyemi
personas.who: 31, warehouse team leader, signing a tenancy agreement the letting agent emailed. Phone-only household — no laptop. Not nervous about tech, just doing this on the move.
personas.context: On the bus at 17:50, phone at 390x844, one thumb, low winter light through a window. He read the hint, rotated the phone to landscape to sign bigger the way it told him to, then rotated back to reach the buttons.
personas.task: Sign the tenancy agreement and email it back before the agent closes at 18:00.
personas.verdict: The file he emailed had his surname missing. He did not find out until the agent replied.
delights: Rotating to landscape does make the pad much bigger — 588px wide against 316px in portrait — and the existing stroke is redrawn rather than wiped, which is more care than the signature_pad issues the research cites ('after you draw your signature and scroll down a little, if you go back up, it vanishes from the canvas').

frictions.what: He signed across a 588px-wide landscape pad, rotated back to portrait to reach Download, and the export silently cropped everything past the new pad width. Measured: signed across ~700 CSS px in landscape, rotated to 390px where the pad is 314px, exported 885x185 — roughly 295 CSS px of ink, so about 57% of the signature was discarded. download() builds its offscreen canvas as `pad.clientWidth * SCALE` (app.js:125) while the stroke points are stored in absolute CSS pixels from whatever width they were drawn at (app.js:22, 80).
frictions.whyItMatters: The app tells him to sign big, landscape is the only way to do that, and rotating back to reach the export button — which is off-screen in landscape anyway (measured at 740x360: pad bottom at 472 against a 360px viewport, padVisible false) — truncates the result. The truncation is visible on the pad for a second before the buttons scroll into view, and the toast still says 'Saved — transparent background, cropped to the ink,' which reads as reassurance. The research asks for exactly this: 'rescale stored strokes proportionally on rotation instead of leaving them in absolute CSS pixels, so a portrait signature is not clipped by a landscape crop.'

frictions.what: In landscape the whole bottom of the signing pad and all three buttons are below the fold (measured at 740x360: pad top 212, pad bottom 472, viewport height 360). There is no full-bleed 'Sign big' mode.
frictions.whyItMatters: The orientation the app pushes him into is the orientation in which he cannot see the bottom of the box he is signing in or the button that finishes the job.

frictions.what: Drawing past the right edge of the pad keeps capturing his finger but stops showing ink. Verified: pointer capture is engaged (app.js:79) so the points keep accumulating off-canvas, the visible stroke stops dead at the border (ink max x = 337 of a 338px buffer), and the export drops everything outside the pad.
frictions.whyItMatters: On a 316px-wide pad with a long surname, running off the edge is the normal case, and the feedback is a stroke that appears to stop rather than a boundary he can feel.

frictions.what: He switched from Medium to Bold after drawing, to see if it looked better, and the exported image changed size without the drawing changing. Measured: same strokes exported 504x180 with Bold selected and 476x152 with Fine selected — a 28px difference — because `padPx = Math.round(size * SCALE * 1.5)` at app.js:159 reads the currently selected pen, not the pens the strokes were actually drawn with.
frictions.whyItMatters: The export is not a deterministic function of the drawing. Changing a control that visibly does nothing quietly changes the file.

worksWell: The core artefact is genuinely excellent and nobody else in the category gets it this right. Decoded pixel by pixel: 93.9% fully transparent, corner alpha 0, exactly one opaque colour (rgb(17,19,24) for black, rgb(29,63,143) for blue — the markup values, unchanged), 1,902 antialiased edge pixels, cropped tight from a 942x780 buffer to 632x216. The research's 'white box' complaint (#3) is solved properly, and trimBounds is unit-tested.

It is a real offline PWA, not a claim. sw.js VERSION sig-v14 precaches all 10 assets; with the network cut the page reloads, draws and exports successfully. 'Turn your Wi-Fi off. It still works' is a statement this app can currently make and prove.

Nothing stands between finishing and the file. No email field, no modal, no rating prompt, no wait timer, no counter, no tip prompt on the export path — the tip link is a header link and stays there. Eight rapid Download clicks produced eight clean files, no double-submit, no corruption, 0 leftover a[download] nodes.

Pointer handling is careful. A second pointer arriving mid-stroke leaves 0 ink in the palm zone. pointercancel commits the in-progress stroke rather than eating it. Resizing the window mid-stroke keeps the stroke and resyncs the backing store. This is more care than most competitors take.

Accessibility of the chrome is clean. axe returned 0 violations in every configuration tested — light, dark, warm tint 3, high contrast, Largest + Roomy, comfort panel open, and after drawing. 12 focusables, 0 unreachable, 0 unnamed, orderly tab order, no traps, real focus rings at 2px solid rgb(96,113,149) / 4.77:1, a <main> landmark, and reduced motion honoured.
Speed is a non-issue. 600 pointer moves in one stroke, full redraw 0.2ms, export 72ms, no jank, zero console errors across every run in this review.
The pad stays a true white rectangle in dark mode (verified rgb(255,255,255) against a rgb(16,20,29) page), which is the correct and deliberate call the research names as a hard constraint.
hurts: The one artefact the user cannot reproduce has no safety net at all: reload loses everything (1,092 ink pixels → 0, 0 bytes of storage), and Clear is an identical-looking full-width button 8px above Download that wipes it instantly with no toast, no confirm and no undo. window.SWS.undo is loaded and never called.

The comfort panel's Spacing control desynchronises the canvas: density=roomy takes the pad from 338px to 320px CSS while the backing store stays 338px, so the pen draws 14px (4.9%) left of the finger and the existing signature squashes. Only Spacing triggers it; only a window resize heals it.

There is no keyboard, switch or screen-reader route to a signature. The canvas has no tabindex, role, label or fallback, and there is no typed path and no photo import — a flat WCAG 2.1.1 failure on the app's only verb.

Rotating from landscape to portrait after signing silently crops the export — measured 57% of the signature discarded — because stroke points are absolute CSS pixels and download() sizes its canvas from the current pad width.

The app never says where a drawn signature is invalid. With the DHS rule effective 10 July 2026 letting USCIS deny a filing and keep the fee, this is the difference between a helpful free tool and one that costs someone real money.

Export is PNG-only with no dimension, dpi or KB control and no readout of any kind. The same gesture yields 633x218 at 414px and 1529x248 at 1280px. The highest-volume signature-upload workflow on earth requires JPG-on-white at exact sizes and this app cannot produce it.

Warm tint paints rgba(255,166,86,0.46) over the WYSIWYG signing pad, rendering it rgb(255,214,177). The user picks an ink colour against a background the file will never have, and the guide marks drop to 1.01:1.

The signing pad is the only element that ignores the comfort settings: hardcoded 260px tall and 244-320px wide at every text size and density, while Largest text pushes the Download button below the fold.
The ruled line and the ✕ — the only wayfinding on the signing surface — are hardcoded hex at 1.37:1 and 1.80:1, and High contrast does not touch them.
In dark mode the black ink swatch is 1.12:1 against the card (invisible as a colour) and the pad is a 18.42:1 white slab.
Ink and pen selection is class-only: no aria-pressed, no group name for 'Ink' and 'Pen', no control ever disabled.
The 30x30px ink swatches never scale and sit 14px under the system's own 44px --tap floor; the pen-weight buttons are 32-33px at default.
Research table stakes entirely absent: typed signature, photo import, SVG export, JPG-on-white, size presets, copy to clipboard, redo, initials, and any persistence — opt-in or otherwise.
The .trust component is defined in this app's own CSS (index.html:437) and never instantiated, in the app where privacy IS the product. No skip link, no <noscript>.
mostWantedNext: A 'Where this works — and where it does not' block, permanently on the page: fine for leases, school forms, vendor paperwork and email footers; not for USCIS filings, wills, adoption papers or court orders, with the print-sign-scan route and a handoff to scan-to-pdf.

Undo on Clear via the SWS.undo runtime that is already loaded, plus a session draft of the strokes array so a reload does not erase the work — paired with a stated, visible 'nothing is kept, on purpose' and a one-tap wipe.

Recompute the canvas on anything that changes its box — a ResizeObserver on the pad rather than a window resize listener — and store stroke points normalised to the pad so rotation rescales instead of cropping.

A typed-signature route with real handwriting faces plus a photo-import route with a threshold control: three keyboard-reachable ways to the same output, which is simultaneously the Section 508 fix, the 'it looks nothing like my signature' fix, and the two biggest table-stakes gaps.

An export panel with a live readout — output px, KB and effective print size in inches at 300 dpi — plus named presets (transparent PNG for documents; 140x60 JPG at 30 KB; 160x60; 3.5 x 1.5 cm; a print preset), and copy-to-clipboard beside Download.
A full-bleed 'Sign big' sheet, and a signing pad that grows with the comfort settings instead of staying at a hardcoded 260px.
Tokenise the pad guides and exempt the pad from the warm-tint overlay, so the ruled line and the ✕ respond to High contrast and the pad stays true white in every theme.

aria-pressed on both control groups, a real group name for Ink and Pen, 44px swatches, aria-hidden on the ✕, a reason attached to each ink colour, and disabled states on Undo and Download when there is nothing to act on.
Variable stroke width from velocity and ev.pressure — which pointermove already receives and discards (app.js:86) — and SVG export from the geometry helpers.js:23 already computes.

scenarios.name: Palm rejection, drawing off the pad edge, and pointer-capture robustness
scenarios.method: Dispatched a primary pointer stroke with a second pointer landing mid-stroke in the palm zone; drew past the right edge with capture engaged; separately dispatched a pointerdown for a pointer id the browser does not consider active.

Pointer capture: `pad.setPointerCapture(ev.pointerId)` at app.js:79 threw NotFoundError as an uncaught pageerror, and because it sits BEFORE `current = {...}` on app.js:80, the whole stroke was lost (0 ink) while activePointer had already been set on app.js:78. audit.dynamicMarkup:
Almost nothing is JS-built — this app's markup is honest, which makes it unusually safe to restyle. What the JS DOES own at runtime is state and geometry, and both are invisible in the source.

(A) Canvas geometry is JS-owned and viewport-dependent. fitCanvas() (app.js:25-31) writes pad.width = round(pad.clientWidth * DPR) and pad.height = round(260 * DPR) as raw attributes; DPR is min(devicePixelRatio, 3) (app.js:18). The element in source carries no width/height attributes at all, so the backing store is 100% a runtime value (measured: 338x260 at 414px/DPR1; 942x780 at 390px/DPR3). It is recomputed ONLY on window resize (app.js:117). Any CSS change that alters the pad's box without a window resize — a padding change, a new max-width, and today the comfort panel's Spacing dial — leaves the backing store stale and puts the ink up to 5% away from the pointer.

(B) Selection state is class-only. wire() (app.js:101-113) does `document.querySelectorAll('.dot').forEach(d => d.classList.toggle('sel', d === dot))` and the same for `.sizes button`. There is no aria-pressed, no aria-checked, no data attribute. Renaming `.sel` in CSS silently removes every selection indicator with no error. Renaming `.dot` or `.sizes` breaks the wiring itself.

(C) The ink palette lives in the markup, not in a palette. `data-color="#111318"` and `data-color="#1d3f8f"` at index.html:1297-1298 are read straight into the drawing state (app.js:104) and are ALSO duplicated as inline `style="background:#111318"` on the same elements. Changing the swatch appearance in CSS without changing data-color makes the preview lie about the export. Pen weights are likewise `data-size="2|3|5"` parsed at app.js:110.

(D) Transient anchor: download() (app.js:164-169) appends a bare <a href download> to document.body, clicks it, and removes it after 300ms. A new `body > *:last-child` or global `a{}` layout rule can make it flash.

(E) The tip link is revealed by removing .hidden (app.js:178), which depends on `.hidden{display:none !important}` at index.html:852 keeping its !important, because .tipbtn sets display:inline-flex.

(F) The comfort chrome is injected, not authored. sws-prefs.js builds button#swsPrefsBtn and inserts it into the first matching header spot (sws-prefs.js:367, 404), and builds the whole <dialog id="swsPrefs"> and appends it to body (sws-prefs.js:331). Neither appears in index.html. sws-prefs.js also writes data-theme / data-text / data-density / data-reading / data-warmth / data-contrast / data-motion onto <html> before first paint.

(G) app.js declares its OWN module-scoped toast() (app.js:8-14) that sets textContent and toggles .show directly, bypassing the shared SWS.toast/SWS.undo runtime that sws-ui.js loads. That is why the toast never carries an Undo even though #toast.act and #toast .undo are fully styled at index.html:784-802.

comfortDefects.issue: The signing pad — the only thing on the page a user has to aim inside — ignores every comfort setting. Measured 244x260 at 320px at both Default and Largest text, and 320x260 at 414px + Roomy. #pad is `height:260px` and fitCanvas hardcodes cssH = 260.
comfortDefects.fix: Drive the pad's height from the scale — height:clamp(200px, calc(260px * var(--ui-scale)), 60vh) — and read the real box in fitCanvas (pad.clientHeight) instead of the literal 260. Then a Largest-text user gets a bigger place to sign, which is the whole point of the setting.

comfortDefects.issue: Changing Spacing to Roomy resizes the pad's CSS box but not its backing store, because fitCanvas is bound only to window resize. Measured: pad 338px → 320px CSS with canvas.width stuck at 338; the pen then draws 14px (4.9%) left of the finger and the existing signature squashes to match.
comfortDefects.fix: Replace the window listener with `new ResizeObserver(fitCanvas).observe(pad)`. It is a one-line change and it also fixes container-query, zoom and address-bar cases the resize event misses.

comfortDefects.issue: The ruled line and the ✕ are hardcoded hex — #d7dde5 at 1.37:1 and #b9c2cc at 1.80:1 against the white pad — so they are the lowest-contrast elements on the page AND unreachable by the Contrast=High setting, which raised the hint paragraph from 5.95:1 to 16.05:1 and left both of these untouched.
comfortDefects.fix: Introduce two pad-local tokens (e.g. --pad-rule, --pad-mark) defined against the white pad rather than the page, and redefine them under :root[data-contrast="more"] to something at 3:1 or better. These are non-text graphical objects, so 3:1 is the WCAG floor and 1.37:1 is not close.

comfortDefects.issue: Warm tint paints rgba(255,166,86,0.46) at z-index 9999 over everything including the white pad, which renders as rgb(255,214,177). The ruled line falls to 1.01:1, the ✕ to 1.33:1, and the blue ink swatch reads as navy-black.
comfortDefects.where: the base body::after overlay against the hardcoded white at index.html:1253
comfortDefects.fix: Exempt the signing surface. Either give .padwrap a higher stacking context than the overlay, or paint the tint with a mask that excludes the pad. The research names a true-white pad in every theme as a hard constraint that overrides fashion, because the pad is a WYSIWYG preview of ink on paper.

comfortDefects.issue: In dark mode the black ink swatch (#111318) is 1.12:1 against the rgb(26,31,40) card — invisible as a colour — and the pad is a 320x260 pure-white slab at 18.42:1 against the page.
comfortDefects.fix: Give .dot a light inner hairline in dark mode so a near-black swatch still reads as a disc, and inset the pad in a --surface-2 frame so the white rectangle is a sheet on a desk rather than a glare panel. Do NOT tint the pad itself.

comfortDefects.issue: The ink swatches are 30x30px and never scale — measured 30x30 at Default, Largest and Roomy on every viewport — against a system floor of --tap: max(44px, calc(44px * var(--ui-scale))). The pen-weight buttons are 32-33px at Default and only reach 43px at Largest.
comfortDefects.where: index.html:1264 (.dot) and index.html:1266 (.sizes button), floor defined at index.html:265
comfortDefects.fix: width/height:var(--tap) on .dot with the colour drawn as an inner disc, and min-height:var(--tap) on .sizes button. Both are 30px of CSS away from correct.

comfortDefects.issue: At Largest text the Download PNG button falls below the fold — measured at 320px/xxl and 414px/xxl+roomy — and in landscape (740x360) the bottom of the signing pad itself is below the fold at y=472.
comfortDefects.where: index.html:1306-1310 (the .row of three buttons); the unused .actionbar sits at index.html:805
comfortDefects.fix: Put Download PNG in the .actionbar so it stays pinned, or make the button row position:sticky at the bottom on short viewports. The comfort setting a low-vision user needs currently hides the app's only output.

comfortDefects.issue: Magic numbers throughout the app layer: gap:14px and margin-top:10px on .opts, padding:4px 10px and border-radius:8px on .sizes button, border-radius:12px on .padwrap (against this skin's --r:8px), and font-size:.85rem on .opts .label. None is on the 4px spacing scale or the type scale, and the label reaches for the legacy --muted alias.
comfortDefects.fix: gap:var(--s3); margin-top:var(--s3); padding:var(--s2) var(--s3); border-radius:var(--r-ctl); font-size:var(--t-xs); color:var(--ink-2). Then the whole toolbar tracks the density and type dials instead of sitting outside them.

comfortDefects.issue: Clear and Download PNG are visually identical — three 316x44 full-width .btn elements 8px apart at 390px — and .btn.danger exists and is unused. The destructive action sits directly in the thumb path to the primary one.
comfortDefects.fix: Give Clear .btn.ghost or .btn.danger, move it out of the primary row (a small text control beside Undo), and never let it share a full-width stack with Download.

comfortDefects.issue: A cold open shows a blank white rectangle with a faint rule and a faint ✕ and no instruction of any kind. The .empty component (glyph, h3, body) is fully styled and unused.
comfortDefects.fix: The pad cannot hold an .empty block without covering the drawing surface, but it can hold a single high-contrast prompt line inside the pad — 'Sign here with your finger' — that clears on first pointerdown. Right now the only onboarding is a 15px hint paragraph BELOW the pad.

comfortDefects.issue: The working card has no heading, so the page's heading outline is h1 → h2 (hero) and nothing over the tool itself. The base's micro-label rule at index.html:463 never fires.
comfortDefects.fix: Add an h2 ('Sign here') — the base renders it as the standard uppercase micro-label and it gives the card an accessible name.

navigationDefects.issue: Nothing is saved and nothing says so. Measured: 1,092 ink pixels before reload, 0 after; localStorage 0 bytes, no keys. No beforeunload guard, no draft, no restore, and no sentence stating that the app keeps nothing.
navigationDefects.where: app.js:22 (strokes is module-scoped only); the whole of app.js has no storage call
navigationDefects.fix: Keep the default — store nothing — but SAY it, as a deliberate position rather than an absent feature: 'This app never keeps your signature. Close the tab and it is gone. That is on purpose.' Then add a session-only draft (sessionStorage of the strokes array) so an accidental reload is survivable, with a one-tap wipe.

navigationDefects.issue: Clear is instant, silent and irreversible on the one artefact the user cannot reproduce. Verified: 1,773 ink pixels → 0, empty toast, no undo affordance, and Undo afterwards restores nothing. window.SWS.undo exists at runtime and is never called.
navigationDefects.where: app.js:115 (`$('clearBtn').addEventListener('click', () => { strokes = []; ... })`); sws-ui.js:130 provides SWS.undo; index.html loads it at 1270
navigationDefects.fix: const gone = strokes; strokes = []; redraw(); SWS.undo('Cleared', () => { strokes = gone; redraw(); }). Five lines, using a runtime that is already on the page.

navigationDefects.issue: No redo and no history. The research's own emotional read is that people draw this four or five times; every discarded attempt is unrecoverable even though the geometry is trivially small.
navigationDefects.fix: Keep a redo stack fed by pop() and by Clear, and consider a strip of the last three attempts as thumbnails — the strokes arrays are a few KB each.

navigationDefects.issue: Undo on an empty pad is a silent no-op and no control is ever disabled, despite .btn[disabled] styling being present. undoBtn, clearBtn and dlBtn all report disabled false at every state.
navigationDefects.fix: Set .disabled on Undo and Clear when strokes.length === 0 and on Download at the same time, updated from a single setControlState() called after every mutation.

navigationDefects.issue: The export tells the user nothing about what they are getting: no dimensions, no KB, no dpi, no physical size, no filename preview, and no format choice. Measured spread for the same gesture: 632x216 / 16.9 KB at 390px, 633x218 / 14.2 KB at 414px, 1529x248 / 34.5 KB at 1280px.
navigationDefects.where: app.js:120-171 (download()); SCALE hardcoded at app.js:123; toDataURL('image/png') at app.js:165
navigationDefects.fix: A readout beside the button ('1,529 x 248 px · 34 KB · about 5 in wide at 300 dpi') recomputed whenever strokes change, plus named presets: transparent PNG for documents, JPG-on-white at 140x60 / 30 KB and 160x60 for exam portals, and a 300 dpi print size. This is the research's single cheapest differentiator.

navigationDefects.issue: No copy to clipboard, no share, and no handoff. download() only builds an <a download>. The fastest routes into Google Docs, Word and an email footer do not exist.
navigationDefects.fix: Add a Copy button using ClipboardItem with the same blob, and navigator.share where available. Online PNG Tools charges money for clipboard, which is the strongest possible argument for giving it away here.

navigationDefects.issue: There is no statement anywhere about where a drawn signature is not valid. No .warn instance exists on the page (the component is defined at index.html:670 and unused).
navigationDefects.where: index.html:1283-1287 (the hero, which is the only place the app talks about itself)
navigationDefects.fix: A permanent 'Where this works — and where it does not' block: fine for leases, school forms, vendor paperwork and email footers; NOT for USCIS filings, wills, adoption papers or court orders. Give the correct route (print, sign in ink, scan) and hand off to scan-to-pdf. The DHS interim final rule effective 10 July 2026 lets USCIS deny a filing for an invalid signature after intake and keep the fee.

navigationDefects.issue: The two ink colours carry no explanation — aria-label 'Black ink' / 'Blue ink' and nothing else, title null on both. Users pick the default and find out later.
navigationDefects.fix: One clause per swatch: black for scanning, printing and exam portals; blue because it proves an original against a photocopy, which lenders and title companies expect. It is free, it is true, and it turns a two-button picker into visible expertise.

navigationDefects.issue: No <noscript>. With JS off the page renders a hero, a blank white rectangle and three dead buttons — indistinguishable from a broken site, on the app whose whole pitch is trustworthiness.
navigationDefects.fix: A <noscript> .warn inside the card: 'This tool runs entirely in your browser and needs JavaScript on. That is also why nothing is uploaded.'

navigationDefects.issue: The .trust component — the studio's privacy stamp — is defined in this app's own CSS and never used. The privacy promise appears only as hero prose and a grey footer line.
navigationDefects.where: defined at index.html:437-448 (with a print override at 1227); the body never instantiates it
navigationDefects.fix: Instantiate .trust directly above the pad with a falsifiable claim rather than an adjective: 'Turn your Wi-Fi off. It still works.' That is verifiable in five seconds and it is currently true (sig-v14 caches all 10 assets; a fully offline reload, draw and export all succeeded).

navigationDefects.issue: Every export is named signature.png with no debounce or busy state; eight rapid clicks produced eight indistinguishable files.
navigationDefects.fix: Name it signature-YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.png (or append the ink colour and size), and disable the button for the duration of the 72ms export.

navigationDefects.issue: The only way back to the studio is a footer link with inline style="color:inherit", which overrides the base's footer.colophon a rule and removes the colour distinction between link and text.
navigationDefects.fix: Delete both inline styles and let index.html:431 apply.

a11yDefects.issue: There is no keyboard, switch or assistive-technology route to producing a signature. <canvas id="pad"> has tabindex null, role null, aria-label null and zero fallback content, and drawing on it is the only path to an output — there is no typed path, no photo import, no file input and no drop target anywhere in the app.
a11yDefects.where: index.html:1291; the pointer handlers at app.js:75-99 are the only input path
a11yDefects.fix: A flat WCAG 2.1.1 failure. Ship the typed-signature route with real handwriting faces and a photo-import route, both keyboard-reachable, and give the canvas role="img" with a live accessible name that describes its current state ('Signature pad — 3 strokes drawn' / 'Signature pad — empty'). Section 508 guidance and ADA practice both name typing and image upload as the required alternatives.

a11yDefects.issue: Ink and pen selection is invisible to assistive technology. Verified: both .dot buttons and all three .sizes buttons have aria-pressed null and role null; state lives only in a CSS class toggled at app.js:105 and app.js:111.
a11yDefects.fix: aria-pressed="true|false" on all five, set in the same toggle. Cheapest correct fix in the app.

a11yDefects.issue: Neither control group has a programmatic name. 'Ink' (index.html:1296) and 'Pen' (index.html:1299) are plain <span class="label"> elements — not legends, not fieldsets, not aria-label or aria-labelledby targets — so a screen reader hears 'Fine, Medium, Bold' with no indication of what they modify.
a11yDefects.fix: Wrap each group in role="group" with aria-labelledby pointing at the existing span, or use two real fieldsets with legends.

a11yDefects.issue: The ✕ guide mark is live text with no aria-hidden (verified null), so it is announced in the middle of the main region where it means nothing.
a11yDefects.fix: aria-hidden="true" on .padx (and on .padline for good measure).

a11yDefects.issue: No skip link, even though the .skip component is fully styled and <main id="main"> exists as a valid target.
a11yDefects.where: unused CSS at index.html:840-849; target present at index.html:1281
a11yDefects.fix: Skip to the signing pad as the first child of body. One line.

a11yDefects.issue: The working card has no accessible name — section.card with no heading — so landmark and heading navigation offer only banner, main, contentinfo and one hero h2.
a11yDefects.fix: Add an h2 to the card, or aria-label the section.

a11yDefects.issue: Non-text contrast failures on the two graphical objects that constitute all the wayfinding on the signing surface: the ruled line at 1.37:1 and the ✕ at 1.80:1 against the white pad (1.01:1 and 1.33:1 with warm tint on). The WCAG 1.4.11 floor for non-text content is 3:1. axe does not catch these because neither is text on a background it evaluates.
a11yDefects.fix: Take both to at least 3:1 against white and make them respond to data-contrast. This is the clearest example in the app of a real failure that a clean axe run does not surface.

a11yDefects.issue: In dark mode the black ink swatch is 1.12:1 against the card, so the control communicates its own colour to nobody. Its aria-label ('Black ink') is correct, which means sighted low-vision users are the ones left out.
a11yDefects.where: index.html:1264 with the dark palette at index.html:103-131
a11yDefects.fix: An inner hairline or a light ring on .dot in dark mode.

a11yDefects.issue: Three targets under the 44px floor at every comfort setting: button.dot 30x30 (never scales), .sizes button 32-33px at Default, and the shared #swsPrefsBtn and a#tipLink at 36px.
a11yDefects.where: index.html:1264, 1266 (app layer) and the base .tipbtn / .btn.icon rules; floor at index.html:265
a11yDefects.fix: var(--tap) on the app-layer controls. The two chrome elements are a base-layer fix affecting all 23 apps.

a11yDefects.issue: No control is ever disabled or marked aria-disabled, so Undo announces as available when it does nothing and Download announces as available with an empty pad. The .btn[disabled] styling exists and is never triggered.
a11yDefects.where: index.html:1261 with no corresponding property set anywhere in app.js
a11yDefects.fix: Toggle the disabled property from a single state function after every mutation; keep the existing toast as the fallback.

a11yDefects.issue: The app defines its own toast() that bypasses the shared runtime, so the styled undo affordance inside the toast can never appear and the toast never carries an action.
a11yDefects.where: app.js:8-14 against sws-ui.js:96 (SWS.toast) and the unused styling at index.html:784-802
a11yDefects.fix: Delete the local toast() and call SWS.toast / SWS.undo. That single change is also what makes the Clear fix possible.

a11yDefects.issue: An uncaught exception can be thrown from inside the pointerdown handler: setPointerCapture is unguarded at app.js:79 while the matching releasePointerCapture at app.js:95 IS wrapped in try/catch. When it throws, execution aborts before `current` is created on the next line, so the stroke is silently lost while activePointer has already been set.
a11yDefects.fix: Wrap it the same way the release is wrapped, and move `current = {...}` above the capture call so a capture failure degrades to drawing-without-capture rather than to no drawing at all.

audit.printSupport:
There is a print block, but it is entirely the shared base layer (index.html:~1180-1237); this app adds zero print CSS of its own and has no Print button.

Is print a core use case? Not directly — the artefact is a PNG that gets pasted into someone else's document. But it matters twice. First, a confused user on a locked-down machine reaches for Ctrl+P. Second, the research's most valuable differentiator (the wet-signature warning) ends with 'print, sign in ink, scan' — so the app should eventually own a print path, just not this one.

What the base gives you, verified under emulateMedia({media:'print'}): header.app hidden, #tipLink hidden, #swsPrefsBtn hidden, footer.colophon hidden, the warm-tint overlay disabled, --ui-scale and --density reset to 1, @page margin 14mm.

What is broken if a user just hits Ctrl+P, all measured:
1. .hero prints — the headline 'Draw it once, use it everywhere' plus the full marketing paragraph, roughly the top third of the sheet.
2. .opts prints — the Ink and Pen toolbar, so the page carries the words 'Ink Pen Fine Medium Bold' next to the signature.
3. Both .dot swatches print as SOLID DARK FILLED CIRCLES. Computed background in print media is rgb(17,19,24). The base's print override at index.html:1221 flattens .btn, .btn.primary, .chip, .seg button — .dot is none of those, so it slips through and wastes ink.
4. All three buttons print as dead controls; none carries .noprint.
5. p.hint prints ('Tip: sign larger than feels natural…').
6. The dashed .padwrap border and its 12px radius print around the signature.
7. The ✕ guide mark prints on top of the signature.
8. The canvas prints at its CSS size — roughly 316 CSS px ≈ 3.3in at 96dpi — from a backing store that may be 3x that, so the printed signature is softer than it needs to be.

What to add: an app-level @media print that hides .hero, .opts, the button row and .hint (add .noprint to each), strips the dashed border and the ✕, and adds a .printonly caption line. Better still, define what printing this page is FOR — the honest answer is a 'sign this in ink' sheet with a ruled box and the document name, which is the wet-signature path the research asks for.
riskyToRestyle: The canvas backing store is JS-owned and depends on the pad's rendered CSS width. fitCanvas (app.js:25-31) sets pad.width = round(pad.clientWidth * DPR) and pad.height = round(260 * DPR), and it runs ONLY on window resize (app.js:117). Any restyle that changes the pad's box without a window resize — new card padding, a max-width, a container query, a density token — desynchronises the pointer from the ink by exactly that ratio. This is not theoretical: the shipped comfort panel's Spacing dial already does it, and the measured error is 14px at 4.9%. Add a ResizeObserver in the same commit as any layout change to .padwrap or section.card.

#pad{height:260px} (index.html:1257) is duplicated as the literal 260 in app.js:27 and again as `off.height = 260 * SCALE` in app.js:126. Change the CSS height alone and the export is drawn against the wrong vertical extent. All three must move together, or better, app.js should read pad.clientHeight.

.padwrap must stay a true white rectangle in every theme (index.html:1253). It is a WYSIWYG preview of ink on paper: a tinted, dimmed or dark-inverted pad makes the exported ink colour a lie. Do not apply filter, opacity, mix-blend-mode or an accent tint to .padwrap or #pad, and note that the base's warm-tint body::after ALREADY violates this at z-index 9999 — fixing that is a fix, not a regression.

The ink palette is hardcoded in the markup in two places on the same elements: data-color="#111318"/"#1d3f8f" (read by app.js:104 and written into every stroke) and inline style="background:#111318"/"#1d3f8f" (what the user sees). Restyling the swatch without changing data-color makes the preview disagree with the file. If the skin's accent becomes the pen — which the research's colorRecommendation asks for — both attributes and app.js's `let color = '#111318'` default (app.js:20) must change together.

Class names the JS depends on: .dot and .sizes button as query targets (app.js:102, 108), .sel as the ONLY selection state (app.js:105, 111), and .hidden with its !important (index.html:852) for the tip link (app.js:178). Renaming any of them breaks behaviour silently with no console error — a permanently unselectable ink or an invisible tip jar.
IDs reached by getElementById: pad, toast, undoBtn, clearBtn, dlBtn, tipLink (app.js:6 and throughout). Wrapping them is safe; renaming or removing any is a hard break.

app.js ships its own toast() (app.js:8-14) that writes textContent and toggles .show directly. It does NOT use the shared SWS.toast, so #toast.act and #toast .undo (index.html:784-802) are dead styling today. If the overhaul changes the toast markup contract, this app will not follow — migrate app.js to SWS.toast in the same commit.

The stylesheet is generated and spliced. Everything between index.html:18 ('▼▼▼ SWS STUDIO BASE') and index.html:1250 ('▲▲▲ END SWS STUDIO BASE ▲▲▲') is written by design/apply.mjs from design/studio.css and design/skins.mjs. Hand-edits inside the markers are destroyed on the next build; app rules must stay below index.html:1252. Note that the app-layer block currently ends the file, so the texture rules at 1240-1249 sit INSIDE the markers while .padwrap sits outside — a restyle that moves the texture must respect that boundary.

Palette values are duplicated outside the stylesheet and will drift: index.html:12-13 (two theme-color metas, #fef6ea / #10141d), manifest.webmanifest (background_color #fef6ea, theme_color #626976 — note this is --accent-fill, not the canvas), icon.svg, apple-touch-icon.png and marketing/thumb-256.png. This app's skin is the near-achromatic one (hue 264 / chroma 0.022) that the research flags as colliding with caregiver-log (250 / 0.035, same warm paper, same editorial voice, same grain texture) — any recolour has to resolve that collision, and the research's recommendation is to separate by value, not hue.

The service worker will serve stale CSS after deploy. sw.js:3 lists a fixed ASSETS array and sw.js:20 is cache-first (`return cached || fetched`), so returning users get the OLD index.html on the first load after a deploy. Any new file — a handwriting font for the typed path, an external stylesheet — must be appended to ASSETS AND VERSION bumped from 'sig-v14' (sw.js:2), or it is never fetched at all offline. Verified in this review: 10 entries cached, full offline reload and export work.

Tests give you almost no safety net. test/helpers.test.mjs covers only the two pure functions in helpers.js — trimBounds and smoothSegments. Nothing touches the DOM, the class names, the stylesheet or the canvas pipeline, so a restyle cannot break the suite and the suite cannot catch a restyle regression. Do not 'simplify' trimBounds' alphaThreshold of 8 (helpers.js:5) — it is what keeps antialiased edge pixels inside the crop, and this review verified 1,902 semi-transparent pixels survive in a real export.

touch-action:none on .padwrap (index.html:1255) is functional, not cosmetic: it is what stops the page scrolling instead of drawing, which is the research's most-cited mobile complaint. Never move it, never let a restyle drop it, and never let a new scroll container swallow it.

fixes.title: Make Clear reversible and stop losing the signature on reload
fixes.rationale: Denise lost her best attempt twice — once to a mis-tap on Clear, once to a reflex refresh. Measured: Clear takes 1,773 ink pixels to 0 with an empty toast, no confirm and no undo, and a subsequent Undo restores nothing; reload takes 1,092 ink pixels to 0 with 0 bytes of storage and no warning. Clear is a 316x44 full-width .btn sitting 8px above the identically styled Download PNG at 390px, and .btn.danger is defined and unused. sws-ui.js is loaded and window.SWS.undo exists at runtime — app.js calls it zero times. Snapshot strokes, clear, then SWS.undo('Cleared', restore); add a sessionStorage draft of the strokes array; restyle Clear out of the primary row; and state the ephemerality out loud rather than leaving it as an absent feature ('This app never keeps your signature. Close the tab and it is gone. That is on purpose.').
fixes.where: apps/signature-maker/app.js:115 (clearBtn handler), app.js:22 (strokes, in-memory only), apps/signature-maker/index.html:1306-1310 (the three-button row), .btn.danger at index.html:580

fixes.title: Recompute the canvas whenever the pad's box changes, not only on window resize
fixes.rationale: Marguerite set Spacing to Roomy and the pen started drawing 14px left of her finger. Isolated and measured: density=roomy alone takes the pad from 338px to 320px CSS while canvas.width stays 338; pen down at x=288 lands ink at x=274, a 4.9% error growing toward the right edge, and any signature already on the pad squashes to match. text=xxl and reading=easy do not trigger it; only Spacing does; only a window resize heals it. This is the comfort panel actively breaking the core interaction for exactly the user it exists to serve. Replace the window listener with a ResizeObserver on the pad — one line — and it also fixes zoom, container-query and address-bar cases.

fixes.title: Stop the export cropping the signature when the phone is rotated
fixes.rationale: Yusuf signed in landscape because the app's own hint told him to sign big, rotated back to reach the Download button (which is below the fold in landscape — measured pad bottom 472 against a 360px viewport), and emailed a file with 57% of his signature missing. Measured: signed across ~700 CSS px on a 588px pad, exported at 390px to 885x185 — about 295 CSS px of ink — with the toast still reading 'Saved'. Stroke points are stored as absolute CSS pixels (app.js:22, app.js:71) while download() sizes its offscreen canvas from the CURRENT pad width. Store points normalised to the pad (0-1) so rotation rescales instead of cropping, or size the export canvas from the actual stroke extent rather than pad.clientWidth.
fixes.where: apps/signature-maker/app.js:125-126 (off.width = pad.clientWidth * SCALE), app.js:69-72 (pos()), app.js:80 and 86 (points pushed in absolute CSS px)

fixes.title: Give the app a route to a signature that does not require a pointing device
fixes.rationale: Ilya could select black ink, choose Bold, tab to Download and press Enter — and get a toast telling him to sign first. Verified: <canvas id="pad"> has tabindex null, role null, aria-label null and zero fallback content, and there is no typed path, no photo import, no file input and no drop target anywhere in the app. Everything else is keyboard-perfect (12 focusables, 0 unreachable, 0 unnamed, real focus rings, axe clean), which makes the one gap total. Flat WCAG 2.1.1 failure; Section 508 guidance names typing and image upload as the required alternatives, and the research's tableStakes lists both as verified gaps. Ship type-a-signature with real handwriting faces plus photo import with a threshold control, both keyboard-reachable, and give the canvas role="img" with a live accessible name.
fixes.where: apps/signature-maker/index.html:1291 (the bare canvas), pointer-only handlers at apps/signature-maker/app.js:75-99

fixes.title: Say where a drawn signature is not valid
fixes.rationale: Hal produced a clean signature and used it on an I-130. Nothing in index.html or app.js says a word about validity, and .warn is defined at index.html:670 and never instantiated. The DHS interim final rule published 11 May 2026 and effective 10 July 2026 amends 8 CFR 103.2(a)(7)(ii)(A) so USCIS may reject OR DENY a filing found to lack a valid signature after it has cleared the Lockbox — retaining the fee, with no post-filing correction — and USCIS explicitly rejects signatures 'generated by software'. Signature-related denials went from 300 in FY2021 to 2,953 in FY2025. A permanent 'Where this works — and where it does not' block: fine for leases, school forms, vendor paperwork and email footers; not for USCIS filings, wills, adoption papers or court orders, with the print-sign-scan route and a handoff to our own scan-to-pdf. Every competitor's incentive is to make you sign; ours is not, and this is the whole value of that asymmetry.
fixes.where: apps/signature-maker/index.html:1283-1287 (the hero is the only place the app talks about itself); unused .warn component at index.html:670

fixes.title: Show what the file will be, and offer JPG-on-white with size presets
fixes.rationale: Priyanka needed 140x60 JPG on white under 30 KB and got a 632x216 transparent PNG at 16.9 KB, with no number shown anywhere. Measured spread for one gesture: 632x216 / 16.9 KB at 390px, 633x218 / 14.2 KB at 414px, 1529x248 / 34.5 KB at 1280px — output size is purely an accident of the browser window, and the 1280px case alone blows the portals' 30 KB ceiling. SCALE is hardcoded to 3 over pad.clientWidth and toDataURL('image/png') is the only output. The research's ranked rejection list is topped by 'Format not JPEG — PNG is commonly rejected' and 'Coloured background instead of white', and complaint #4 (Adobe's documented Fill & Sign blur) means the only defence we control is giving people more pixels and telling them the number. Add a live readout (px, KB, inches at 300 dpi) recomputed on every stroke change, plus named presets and a JPG-on-white variant labelled with why.
fixes.where: apps/signature-maker/app.js:120-171 (download()), SCALE at app.js:123, format at app.js:165

fixes.title: Let the signing pad grow with the comfort settings, and keep Download on screen

fixes.title: Make the ink and pen controls speak, and attach a reason to each colour
fixes.rationale: Ilya heard five anonymous buttons; Hal picked black for a mortgage package the title company wants in blue. Verified: both .dot buttons and all three .sizes buttons have aria-pressed null and role null, with selection living only in classList.toggle('sel'); 'Ink' and 'Pen' are plain spans, not legends; title is null on both swatches. The research calls this free, true, and the thing that turns a two-button picker into visible expertise.

fixes.rationale: Marguerite turned Warm tint up for window glare and the pad rendered rgb(255,214,177) — measured off a real screenshot — because body::after paints rgba(255,166,86,0.46) at z-index 9999 over the hardcoded-white .padwrap. fixes.title: Take the ruled line and the ✕ to a legible contrast and let High contrast reach them
fixes.rationale: These two marks are the entire wayfinding of the signing surface and they are the lowest-contrast elements on the page: #d7dde5 at 1.37:1 and #b9c2cc at 1.80:1 against the white pad, against a WCAG 1.4.11 floor of 3:1 for non-text graphical objects. fixes.title: Guard setPointerCapture, refuse to export a stray dot, and stop the pen size changing the exported margins
fixes.rationale: Three small correctness bugs found by driving the export. (1) setPointerCapture at app.js:79 is unguarded while the matching release at app.js:95 IS wrapped in try/catch; when it throws, execution aborts before `current` is created on the next line, so the stroke is silently lost, an uncaught NotFoundError hits the console, and activePointer stays set until a matching pointerup clears it. Reproduced with a synthetic pointer, latent for real input. (2) A single tap exports a 38x38 / 411-byte PNG with the toast 'Saved — transparent background, cropped to the ink' — the only guard is strokes.length === 0 at app.js:121, and Priyanka got one at 23:20 with a deadline. (3) padPx reads the CURRENTLY selected pen rather than the strokes' own sizes, so the same drawing exported 504x180 with Bold selected and 476x152 with Fine selected — a 28px difference from a control that appears to do nothing.
